sections.content:
Population change in Worcester in 2032

The population in Worcester is projected to increase from 104,119 people in 2022 to 105,107 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 4,644 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Worcester
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Worcester, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 618, with 9,508 births and 10,126 deaths in Worcester between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Worcester by 0.6%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 2,347, with 68,511 people moving to the area and 70,858 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Worcester by 2.3%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 676, with 3,419 people moving to the area and 4,095 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Worcester by 0.6%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4,644, with 10,116 people moving to the area and 5,472 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Worcester by 4.5%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Worcester in 2032

The median age in Worcester is projected to rise from 40 years in 2022 to 42 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 20% of the population in Worcester are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 17% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Worcester between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Worcester is projected to stay the same, at around 65%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 260 to 289 over the same time period.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Worcester?

In 2032, 18% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Worcester between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
